title: Cooperative blocked KV allocator and GPU swap/throttle prototype
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Background: We observe tail latency regressions when the KV resident set outgrows GPU DRAM under mixed short/long sequence workloads. Current slab-based approaches either cause expensive synchronous swaps or evict hot KV entries, degrading generation quality and increasing cost due to rewarm. Goal: Prototype a cooperative 'blocked' KV allocator that divides KV storage into fixed-size pages and coordinates eviction/throttling with the continuous batching runtime to avoid synchronous swap stalls and reduce overall token latency variance.

Scope: implement a prototype allocator and runtime hooks to: 1) allocate KV in pages (configurable page size), 2) maintain a lightweight residency bitmap and LRU-like ranking per-page, 3) expose a throttle window to the batch scheduler for backpressure, and 4) implement an async GPU->host pinned swap path with predictive prefetch hints from the KV admission path. This prototype is focused on behavior and metrics; final kernel tuning and custom memcpy kernels will come later.

Key ideas: 
- Blocked pages: map KV entries (kv blocks) into contiguous page slots to reduce fragmentation and enable coarse-grained residency accounting.
- Cooperative throttling: when estimated resident pages < active working set, the runtime signals a throttle window (short delay allowed) to the batching layer instead of immediately performing blocking device-host swaps. This reduces synchronous-blocking for many short requests and shifts burden to queueing which is cheaper when sequences are short.
- Predictive prefetch: use a lightweight access-frequency sketch per-key to mark candidates for prefetch into GPU when a request touches a neighboring key or when a route historically shows long context lengths.
- Async swap path: move evicted pages to host-pinned buffers and mark them as eligible for background upload. If a hot request needs a page that's currently on host, the scheduler can either: a) block for a small bounded time to allow a fast pinned transfer, b) fall back to a smaller model variant, or c) serve degraded quality (partial KV) depending on route policy.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Coarse pages reduce metadata overhead but increase chance of moving slightly more data on eviction. We picked page sizes between 64KB and 256KB for experimentation.
- Throttle windows introduce small latency tail for some requests but greatly reduce worst-case head-of-line blocking under bursty traffic.
- Predictive prefetch reduces blocking at cost of extra memory movement; we will cap prefetch budget per-cycle.

Success metrics: lower p99 token latency under mixed-traffic benchmarks, reduction in synchronous DMA stalls, and no regression in generation quality (per-prompt score). Also track increased host<->GPU traffic and ensure it stays within acceptable thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype allocator merged to feature branch with flags to opt-in
Integration test that simulates mixed short/long sequence traffic shows >=30% reduction in synchronous swap stalls compared to baseline
p99 token latency improvement on our production-like benchmark (same traffic mix) or equivalent decrease in tail variance without quality regression
Fallback behaviors (model-variant fallback and blocked serve timeout) are exercised in integration tests
Observability: residency metrics, page move counters, and throttle-window signals exposed to Console tracing
benchmarks_summary: Local lab runs (A100 80GB) with synthetic mix: 70% short (<=64 tokens) 30% long (>=1024 tokens). Baseline slab allocator: observed frequent blocking spikes correlated with large sequential long requests, p99 token latency 420ms. Blocked allocator prototype (page=128KB, throttle-window=8ms): synchronous swap stalls reduced by 42%, p99 token latency 280ms, median unchanged. Host<->GPU bandwidth increased by ~18% due to prefetch budget (config capped). Note: numbers are from early prototype without optimized memcpy kernels; expect further gains after kernel-level optimizations.

2026-03-08 - Marco: Implemented predictive prefetch sketch using a 4-bit decay counter per key and a global prefetch budget. Nightly runs show improved rare long-request cases with minimal extra traffic.

rollout_plan: 1) Keep feature gated off by default. 2) Enable in internal staging with small fleet (5% of internal traffic) and monitoring alarms for page-move rate and p99 token latency. 3) If stable for 48h, enable 25% canary on production consumer routes with opt-in via deployment flag. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% per-customer with route-level opt-outs and a fast rollback flag. 5) After stability, iterate on kernel memcpy and page-size tuning in follow-up tickets.
